source: NCERT Class XI, Statistics for Economics, Ch. 7 (Index Numbers).

sections.heading: 1. Meaning of Index Numbers
points: An **index number** = a statistical device that measures the **relative change** in a variable (or group of variables) over time, place or other characteristics.
It expresses change **relative to a base period** (base = 100).
Used to measure changes in **prices, production, cost of living, etc.**

sections.heading: 2. Construction of Index Numbers
points: Choose a **base year** (a normal year, value = 100).
**Simple index** — for a single item; **weighted/aggregative index** — for a group, giving weights (quantities) to items.
**Laspeyres index** (base-year quantities as weights) and **Paasche index** (current-year quantities) are common methods.
**Price relative = (current price ÷ base price) × 100**.

sections.heading: 3. Important Index Numbers in India
points: **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** — measures change in the **cost of living** / retail prices for consumers; used to calculate **inflation and dearness allowance**.
**Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** — change in **wholesale prices**; a measure of inflation.
**Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** — change in industrial output.
**Sensex/Nifty** — stock market indices.
**Human Development Index (HDI)** — a composite index of well-being.

sections.heading: 4. Uses and Limitations
points: **Uses:** measure **inflation**, adjust wages/pensions, frame policy, compare across time/regions.
**Limitations:** choice of base year and items affects results; can be manipulated; represents averages (not every individual).
Index numbers are called 'economic barometers'.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Index number = measures relative change over time (base = 100).
Price relative = (current price ÷ base price) × 100.
CPI = cost of living/retail prices; WPI = wholesale prices; both measure inflation.
IIP = industrial production; Sensex/Nifty = stock market.
Index numbers = 'economic barometers'.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: In an index number, the **base period value = 100**.
**CPI = consumer/retail (cost of living)**; **WPI = wholesale prices**.
**CPI is used to compute dearness allowance and consumer inflation**.
Index numbers measure **relative change** (not absolute values).
